title: To amend title 5, United States Code, to expand law enforcement availability pay to employees of U.S. Customs and Border Protection's Air and Marine Operations.
official_summary:
(This measure has not been amended since it was introduced. The summary of that version is repeated here.)

This bill applies provisions governing availability pay for criminal investigators to any employee of the U.S. Customs and Border Protection's Air and Marine Operations who is a law enforcement officer.

summary.headline: This law extends the extra pay rules used for criminal investigators to law enforcement officers in U.S. Customs and Border Protection's Air and Marine Operations.
summary.what_it_does: The law changes federal pay rules in Title 5 of the U.S. Code. It applies the availability pay provisions that cover criminal investigators to any Air and Marine Operations employee who is a law enforcement officer. Availability pay is extra pay tied to being available for unscheduled work. The summary does not give the pay rate or conditions.

who_it_affects.group: Law enforcement officers in U.S. Customs and Border Protection's Air and Marine Operations
who_it_affects.how: They become eligible for the same availability pay that applies to criminal investigators.
The agency's pay costs for these officers change because of the new eligibility.

summary.when_it_takes_effect: The law was enacted on December 8, 2016. The summary does not list a separate effective date.
